description: This line plot illustrates the similarity scores across different model layers for four language pair combinations: en&en (red solid line), en&es (blue solid line), en&el (green solid line), and en&bn (magenta dashed line), as evaluated in the context of layer-wise mixture-of-experts for multilingual LLM expansion. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 22 with integer tick marks at every 2 units, representing discrete transformer layers. The y-axis, labeled “Similarity,” ranges from 0.00 to 0.45 with tick marks at intervals of 0.05, indicating the degree of similarity (likely between representations or attention patterns). All four lines exhibit non-monotonic behavior: they generally rise from layer 0 to a peak around layer 6–7 (with en&en reaching ~0.26, en&es ~0.24, en&el ~0.15, en&bn ~0.14), then decline gradually until layer 20–21, where they all dip to near-minimum values (~0.04–0.06). From layer 22 onward, all lines surge sharply, with en&en rising steeply to ~0.44, en&es to ~0.27, en&el to ~0.30, and en&bn to ~0.29, suggesting a significant increase in similarity at the final layers. The red en&en line consistently remains above the others across most layers, especially after layer 22, while the magenta en&bn line generally tracks below the green en&el and blue en&es lines until the final surge.
